rows.doi_or_pmid: not reported (no DOI or PMID printed on the article); J Pak Assoc Dermatol 2023;33(4):1353-1358
rows.design: descriptive longitudinal study, single arm, uncontrolled
rows.body_site: lower limbs 72.7%, upper limbs 18.2%, trunk 9.1% (denominator not reported; [the shares equal 32, 8 and 4 of 44 patients, not shares of the 200 macules])
rows.skin_tone: not reported (study in Mandya, India; Fitzpatrick type not given)
rows.lesions_enrolled: [220] not reported directly; inferred as five macules per recruited patient
rows.analysis_unit: lesion (macule); five macules per patient analysed as independent
rows.intervention: 308 nm excimer laser (Excimal Elite), twice weekly for 12 weeks, start 250 mJ/cm2, plus 50 mJ/cm2 every week until perifollicular or marginal pigmentation; stopped at complete resolution or after maximum 24 sessions
rows.comparator: none (no control macules, no untreated arm)
rows.assessment_method: physician quartile grading scale (Grade 0 none, 1-25% minimal, 26-50% moderate, 51-75% good, >75% excellent) using serial photographs and DermLite DL3N dermoscopy; blinding and number of assessors not reported
rows.complete_match: not reported (treatment stopped at complete resolution, but the number of macules that reached it is not given)
rows.texture_or_scar: not reported (erythema and burning sensation were monitored; no counts given)
rows.citation: Deepadarshan K, Shashi Kumar BM, Harish MR, Meghana BC. Dermoscopic evaluation of efficacy of 308 nm Excimer Laser in treatment of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis - A descriptive longitudinal study. J Pak Assoc Dermatol 2023;33(4):1353-1358
rows.endpoint_definition: share of macules in each physician improvement grade; excellent = >75% improvement (partial repigmentation, not complete coverage)
rows.uncertainty: Uncontrolled; five macules per patient treated as independent. Table 1 'Minimal' appears to pool Grade 0 and Grade 1 (the Methods scale has both). Methods list photographs and dermoscopy only to week 12; Results add a week 16 dermoscopy visit. Body-site percentages are said to describe macules, but their denominator is not reported and they match [32, 8 and 4 of 44 recruited patients]. The authors list 'the limited sample size and short follow-up period' as limitations.

rows.uncertainty: Uncontrolled; five macules per patient treated as independent. Table 1 'Minimal' appears to pool Grade 0 and Grade 1 (the Methods scale has both). Methods list photographs and dermoscopy only to week 12; Results add a week 16 dermoscopy visit. Follow-up length conflicts within the paper: Methods say patients were followed for 1 month after treatment, Results speak of 'the 4-month follow-up period' and PIH persisting 'at 4th month of follow up', which matches 16 weeks counted from baseline. months_after_final_tx 1 is the Methods statement; it equals [4 weeks] after a full 12-week course, and for macules stopped early at complete resolution the interval is longer and not reported. Recurrence: 'None of the repigmented macules showed reappearance of depigmentation' at this visit (about one month after treatment). Abstract and Results give the week 16 distribution as the study result. Body-site percentages are said to describe macules, but their denominator is not reported and they match [32, 8 and 4 of 44 recruited patients]. The authors list 'the limited sample size and short follow-up period' as limitations.
